title: First Tor is additive in its second argument
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and M an R-module. Let F be the functor N ↦ Tor'_1(M,N) on the category of R-modules, with Tor' derived in its first argument [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. For any R-modules X,Y and R-linear maps f,g : X → Y, F(f+g)=F(f)+F(g); equivalently F is additive.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 00MM (lemma-surjective-on-tor-one), functorial coefficient action in the free-resolution proof; supporting resolution computation formalized in Sheaf.RingTheory.TorOneSurjectiveFlatMiddle

proof.text: Fix the projective resolution P of M once for all coefficient modules. By the definition of Tor' and Mathlib ProjectiveResolution.leftDerived_app_eq, its map on a coefficient homomorphism f is the degree-one homology map of P tensor f, conjugated by the fixed comparison isomorphisms for the source and target. These isomorphisms depend on the objects, not on f.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 00MM (lemma-surjective-on-tor-one), functorial coefficient action in the free-resolution proof; supporting resolution computation formalized in Sheaf.RingTheory.TorOneSurjectiveFlatMiddle

proof.text: Tensoring on the right sends f+g to the sum of the corresponding natural transformations (Functor.map_add). Evaluation of mapHomologicalComplex on P preserves that sum, as seen degreewise by extensionality. Homology is an additive functor, so its induced map on the sum is the sum of its maps. Composition with the two fixed comparison morphisms distributes over addition (Preadditive.add_comp and Preadditive.comp_add). This proves F(f+g)=F(f)+F(g) for every X,Y,f,g, and supplies Functor.Additive.
